text:
## Compensation Framework  
**Financial Compensation Guidelines:**  
| Scenario | Compensation Range | Basis |
|----------|-------------------|-------|
| Service delay (1–2 days) | £0–£50 | Inconvenience |
| Service delay (3–5 days) | £50–£100 | Operational disruption |
| Service failure (>5 days) | £100–£300 | Significant impact |
| Financial loss (error) | Full loss + 8% interest | Actual loss + interest |
| Serious distress | £250–£500+ | Emotional impact |  
**Limits (aligned with Escalation Matrix above):**
- <£500: Complaints Manager approval
- £500–£2,000: Director approval
- >£2,000: CEO approval
- >£5,000: Board notification + CEO approval

raw_entities.name: Compensation Framework
raw_entities.description: Establishes the bank's formal financial compensation standards for customer service failures, delays, losses, and distress. Defines monetary ranges based on impact severity and outlines the hierarchical approval matrix required to authorize payments exceeding specific thresholds.

raw_entities.name: Service Delay Compensation (1–2 Days)
raw_entities.description: Mandates a financial compensation range of £0–£50 for service delays lasting between one and two days. This provision recognizes baseline customer inconvenience and establishes a fixed operational standard for minor service disruptions.

raw_entities.name: Service Delay Compensation (3–5 Days)
raw_entities.description: Requires a compensation range of £50–£100 for service delays extending from three to five days. The provision accounts for operational disruption experienced by the customer and scales financial redress accordingly.

raw_entities.name: Service Failure Compensation (>5 Days)
raw_entities.description: Stipulates a compensation range of £100–£300 for service failures lasting more than five days. This rule reflects the significant impact on customer operations and mandates higher financial redress for prolonged disruptions.

raw_entities.name: Financial Loss Compensation
raw_entities.description: Requires full reimbursement of actual financial losses caused by bank errors, plus an additional 8% interest. This provision ensures complete monetary restoration for customers affected by processing mistakes or accounting discrepancies.
context: Financial loss (error) | Full loss + 8% interest | Actual loss + interest

raw_entities.name: Serious Distress Compensation
raw_entities.description: Authorizes a compensation range of £250–£500 or more for cases resulting in serious emotional distress. The provision acknowledges non-financial customer impact and permits elevated redress when severe psychological harm is documented.

raw_entities.name: Compensation Approval Thresholds
raw_entities.description: Establishes a hierarchical approval matrix for compensation payments, requiring Complaints Manager approval for amounts under £500. Director approval is mandated for £500–£2,000, CEO approval for over £2,000, and Board notification plus CEO approval for amounts exceeding £5,000.

raw_entities.name: Complaints Manager
raw_entities.description: Holds the authority to approve financial compensation claims up to £500 under the bank's escalation and approval framework. This role is responsible for validating service failure redress within the lower monetary threshold.

raw_entities.name: Director
raw_entities.description: Responsible for authorizing compensation payments ranging from £500 to £2,000 as part of the bank's financial control escalation matrix. The role ensures mid-tier service failure claims receive appropriate executive oversight.

raw_entities.name: CEO
raw_entities.description: Required to approve compensation amounts exceeding £2,000 and must be involved in the approval process for claims over £5,000. The role provides executive sign-off for high-value financial commitments and severe service failures.

raw_entities.name: Board
raw_entities.description: Must be formally notified when any single compensation claim exceeds £5,000 to ensure oversight of high-value financial commitments. The provision mandates board-level awareness for extreme service failures or significant customer losses.
